title.value: Electrochemical Nitrate Reduction Reaction to Ammonia at Industrial-Level Current Densities.

abstract.value: The electrochemical nitrate reduction reaction (NO<sub>3</sub> <sup>-</sup>RR) represents a promising green synthesis technology, enabling both resource utilization of nitrate (NO<sub>3</sub> <sup>-</sup>) pollutants in wastewater and provision of a sustainable ammonia (NH<sub>3</sub>) source for carbon neutrality. The key challenge in advancing NO<sub>3</sub> <sup>-</sup>RR toward practical application lies in developing catalytic systems that maintain excellent activity, high selectivity, and long-term stability at industrial-level current densities (>300 mA cm<sup>-2</sup>). Although NO<sub>3</sub> <sup>-</sup>RR has been developed to a certain extent, there has yet to be a comprehensive summary and analysis of the advancements in this field at industrial-level current densities up to now. This review begins with an introduction to the mechanism and theoretical basis of NO<sub>3</sub> <sup>-</sup>RR, systematically summarizes and analyzes catalyst design strategies for industrial-level current densities, including alloying methods, in situ derivation strategy, heterostructure construction, doping engineering, and self-supporting electrode fabrication.
